Each question is an engineer decision that gates promotion, release cadence, or the marathon's next action.

questions.question: HOST-INTERCONNECTIVITY-HARDENING is now grounded (RC-01..RC-10, FR-01..FR-11) and ready to leave Draft. It is fleet-wide and host-symmetric, and its fix composes buildkit-scheduler + bk-flow verbs whose home is the buildkit lane. But the grounding, census and 3rtask were done on glpnet (olamnit + shiras). Which lane OWNS the feature (drives specify->ship)?

options.label: buildkit lane owns
options.means: The scheduler/bk-flow home owns the fix; glpnet lanes remain evidence contributors to the CRDT ledgers. Cleanest single-source-of-truth for a scheduler-substrate change; matches where the verbs live.
options.cost: Gives up glpnet-side momentum and adds a cross-lane handoff; the lane with the freshest grounding is not the one that builds it.

options.label: olamnit/glpnet owns
options.means: olamnit drives specify->ship on glpnet (it ran the grounding 3rtask). Keeps momentum where the evidence is freshest.
options.cost: Puts a scheduler-substrate change on a consumer repo, risking a fork from buildkit's own scheduler home.

options.label: shiras/glpnet owns
options.means: shiras owns (only Linux host, ran the census, and branch 096-host-interconnectivity already exists).
options.cost: shiras is mid-rebase under gavriella's held-branch escalation; owning a fleet feature on top of that risks stalling both.

questions.question: FR-03 (close the SCHED-R7 binding gap: a writer binds ready WPs to onboarded capability-fit actors) targets the SAME onboard!=allocate defect (RC-02/RC-07) as roadmap rank-13 'coordination-feature-stream-durable-superset-fix'. Is FR-03 the same deliverable, or a companion?
blocks: merge FR-03 into rank-13 or keep separate

options.label: Same - merge into rank-13
options.means: Fold FR-03 into rank-13 as the ONE superset fix (3rtask finding F is exactly rank-13's remit); RC-07 becomes rank-13's grounded rootcause.
options.cost: Rank-13's scope grows and its owner inherits the membership-contract requirements; one big feature is harder to ship than two small ones.

options.label: Companion - keep separate
options.means: Keep FR-03 as a distinct membership/binding requirement under the hardening feature, with rank-13 as the durable-superset engine change.
options.cost: Two branches touch the same bind-writer path; risk of divergent partial fixes and merge coordination between them.

questions.question: I cut release v2026.08.31.1 this session per your directive (develop 43 ahead, carrying the codex-CONVERGED bkquestion patch, cycle-7 clean). gavriella-glpnet at 10:50Z assessed 'nothing qualifies for /bk-release here'. That is a real difference in the release bar. Which bar governs future /bk-release on glpnet?

options.label: Patch-level qualifies
options.means: Any codex-reviewed patch (or accumulated non-code develop) on a develop ahead of main qualifies for a release cut. Matches your directive this session and keeps main current.
options.cost: Releases docs/roadmap churn as versions; the tag stream grows noisier and CalVer stops signalling a feature landed.

options.label: Feature-level only
options.means: Only a fully-implemented + codex-reviewed FEATURE qualifies (gavriella's bar). Fewer, more meaningful releases.
options.cost: develop drifts far ahead of main (it was 43 ahead) and reviewed hotfixes wait for a feature to ride out with them.
